title: fix: reclaim captures beside unreadable macOS processes
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Doctor skipping legacy plugin capture cleanup when macOS denies access to another account's process arguments.

Closes #159112. Thanks @bdjben for the NoMachine, Logitech, and softwareupdated reproduction evidence.

## User Impact

`openclaw doctor --fix` can reclaim eligible captures despite unreadable arguments from foreign-UID processes. Same-UID or unknown-UID uncertainty still preserves legacy captures. Doctor also preserves foreign-owned capture directories, including when run with elevated privileges.

Managed native cleanup uses recorded custody and installed-index references without a host-wide argv veto. Cleanup failures remain advisory. No configuration, CLI options, dependencies, database schemas, or update snapshot/rollback behavior change.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Darwin reader previously required a narrow executable-path and Apple-signature fallback after `KERN_PROCARGS2` failed. Third-party daemons and Apple `.app` services fell outside it and blocked the complete Doctor census. The reader now uses the observed UID boundary and records the exclusion once at debug level. Calls without a supplied UID, including Gateway lock inspection, stay conservative.

The legacy deletion owner rechecks directory ownership alongside current identity and maintenance authority. This prevents a privileged Doctor from deleting another user's legacy capture after excluding that user's unreadable process. Managed native captures keep the existing custody and loaded-module owner from #158950; no parallel holder registry is introduced.

## Evidence

Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m3g8ea6c1m8kctneptkb7v9e`, [run 36286350946](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36286350946), Linux x64, Node 24.19.0, pnpm 12.4.2. The wrapper verified source tree `3bedf556fea730e90b22714c929a8aca02136839` and file hashes before execution.

- **104 tests across five touched suites passed three times:** 20.606s, 19.102s, and 19.986s wall.
- **244 tests across 12 files passed** in original importer order plus native-load/startup siblings: 31.962s wall.
- The legacy cleanup regression fails on the original production files while its same-UID control passes. The foreign-owned capture regression fails when only the new directory-ownership guard is removed. The native-custody and errno 1/13/22 regressions also failed on the original code.
- Final macOS Doctor-flow proof: **19 tests passed**, 32.41s wrapper wall / 25.64s Vitest duration, dominated by compiler preparation; test execution was about 1% of the file duration.
- Live read-only macOS syscall probe: exact self argv verified; 366 foreign processes inspected, 365 unreadable foreign processes excluded, zero inspection errors. No Gateway or real capture directory was modified.
- Fresh Codex P1 autoreview: **scoped-clean** after fixing the privileged foreign-directory deletion finding.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs`: **passed**, 1,270.683s wall, including core typechecking, all 25 test type graphs, lint, dead-export scans, schema guards, and import-cycle checks. An earlier pass completed core and all 25 test type graphs, then exposed a test-fixture class-spread lint error; the fixture now forwards module exports through a proxy.

Standalone changed-file costs, each with `pnpm test <file> --maxWorkers=1` on the Testbox:

| File | Tests | Wall | Longest test |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `src/process/supervisor/darwin-process-command.test.ts` | 17 | 1.538s | 2ms |
| `src/plugins/plugin-source-capture-recovery.test.ts` | 12 | 15.408s | 404ms |
| `src/flows/doctor-plugin-source-captures.test.ts` | 19 | 15.382s | 141ms |

The two worker-backed files each spent about 11 seconds preparing shared compiler outputs. No test exceeded 30 seconds or file exceeded 120 seconds of test execution.

LOC: production +23/−49 (net −26); tests +139/−65 (net +74); docs +7/−1. Auto-merge stays off.
